chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'The creatures are My dependants, and the most beloved of them to Me is the most kind to them and the most striving regarding their needs.'

key_terms.عِيَالِي: My dependants / those under my care

ai.seo_question: What quality makes a person most beloved to God according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi from al-Kafi establishes a theological link between divine love and social responsibility, framing all creation as God's dependants ('iyāl) to be cared for. It underscores the Shia emphasis on active benevolence, where the measure of one's closeness to God is determined by one's diligence in alleviating the needs of others, reflecting the concept of 'Ihsan' in interpersonal relations.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Ibn Sinan who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The creatures are My<sup>azwj</sup> dependants, and the most Beloved of them to me it the most kind of them and the most striving of them regarding their needs’.
